question.text: Per the chapter, in case of a deviation of MORE THAN what percentage between two consecutive valuations at the asset level, must the Investment Manager inform investors with reasons?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'At each asset level, in case of deviation in valuation of more than 20% between two consecutive valuations or a deviation of more than 33% in a financial year, the Investment Manager shall inform the investors with reasons for the same.' The Trap: 5% and 10% are too tight; 50% is too loose. Precise regulation says >20% consecutive, >33% FY. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D test the 20%/33% thresholds identically.
